intro: Exact phrase matching is useful for dictionary-based tagging and transparent retrieval filters. Keeping tokens separate avoids accidental substring matches inside words.
task: Find all overlapping token starts matching a phrase without case normalization.
requirements: tokens and phrase are sequences of strings; phrase must be nonempty. Return every zero-based start index where consecutive tokens exactly match the phrase. Include overlapping matches and preserve case. Empty tokens may occur as ordinary token values.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Advance one token after each candidate, even after a successful match.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Compare token slices instead of joining text, which can erase token boundaries.

explanation: Exact phrase matching is useful for dictionary-based tagging and transparent retrieval filters. Keeping tokens separate avoids accidental substring matches inside words.
Overlapping matches are valid occurrences. Jumping ahead by the phrase length after a match would miss repeated-token patterns.
